clue.text: Tell extremely equivocal judge to go outside

indicators.note: the judging word is placed around the other piece

parts.note: to judge is to rate or assess

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of the word equivocal are wanted

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to tell a judge who keeps hedging to step outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge' looks like the definition, but 'Tell' is; 'extremely' wants only the ends of 'equivocal', and 'to go outside' wraps the judging word round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or recount it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Second hare chewed prune

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters of prune are mixed up

explanation.surface: A hare munching on a prune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hare' looks like a noun but is the verb to run.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who finishes second in a race is the one placed just behind the winner.

clue.text: One going places has look at Italian lake and hill

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
Lake Como is in northern Italy
a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A traveller looks at an Italian lake and a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that moves about under its own power is a locomotor, literally a mover from place to place.

clue.text: Minute semi-desert's abandoned fate

indicators.note: 's means has here, and the half-word has been dropped from the word for fate

parts.note: destiny is fate
half of the word desert gives its first three letters

explanation.surface: A tiny, half-dry place has met its doom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-desert' gives DES, half of DESERT; it is removed from DESTINY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minute (pronounced my-NEWT) is extremely small.

clue.text: Hand over drills — less one if gear has odd parts missing

indicators.note: less means minus: the letter for one is taken away

parts.note: to drill soldiers is to train them, so drills gives trains
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the words if gear are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A mechanic's instruction: pass over the drills, one fewer, if the gearbox is missing some parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' drops I from TRAINS to leave TRANS; 'has odd parts missing' keeps the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'if gear', F, E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer something is to pass it to another person, which is handing it over.

clue.text: Runs at Longchamp and is second, so tries again

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
Longchamp is a Paris racecourse, so the French word for and, et, is wanted
est is French for is, carrying on the Longchamp hint

explanation.surface: A horse runs at Longchamp, finishes second, and goes again.
explanation.walkthrough: Longchamp is a racecourse in Paris, pointing to French: ET for 'and', EST for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retest something is to test it again, and testing is trying.

clue.text: Light right above, sound on, any problem?

indicators.note: a problem suggests something to be worked out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A technician asks if there's any problem with the sound being on.
explanation.definitionFit: At midday the sun stands overhead, so its light comes from directly above.

clue.text: Shot rifle one puts away

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters of rifle are scrambled

explanation.surface: A shot rifle being put away by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A filer is a person who files papers, putting them away in order.

clue.text: Pressure to stop attacks which could mean danger down-river

indicators.note: to stop is to plug, so the letter goes inside the attacking word

parts.note: raids are attacks
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Pressure to stop attacks that threaten people downstream.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast, turbulent stretches of water are a hazard to boats heading downstream.

clue.text: Wine retains goodness for minutes

indicators.note: the wine word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: red is wine
cor is a British exclamation like goodness!

explanation.surface: Wine that keeps its goodness for a few minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: COR, like 'goodness!', is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting minutes are the written account of proceedings, an official record.

clue.text: Easy choice read back during trial phase

indicators.note: the word for read is taken backwards

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read carefully
on can mean during, as in on the day
a test is a trial stage

explanation.surface: A choice that is easy to make, read again during a testing phase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read' is the old verb con, to study; 'back' turns it round. A contest with no doubt about the result is an easy call.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest whose result is never in doubt is called this, so it is an obvious, easy pick.

clue.text: Plant beef cheek

parts.note: an ox is a beef animal
lip means cheek, insolent talk

explanation.surface: A butcher's cut: beef cheek, presented as if a plant were involved.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a woodland flower of the primrose family, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Trees he climbs regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words he climbs

explanation.surface: A boy who climbs trees as a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a familiar kind of broadleaf tree, so they are an example of trees.

clue.text: Rated second ride awful

indicators.note: an awful ride is a mess, so the letters of second ride are jumbled

explanation.surface: A racing judgement: the second ride was rated awful.
explanation.definitionFit: To have considered something good is to have rated or regarded it so.

clue.text: Minute odds fixed, so got off horse

indicators.note: fixed odds suggests rigging, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jockey dismounts after learning the tiny odds were fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismount is to climb down from a saddle, so this means got off a horse.

clue.text: I turned around, being inexperienced

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of I turned are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to turning round because they were a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not yet tested in practice is a novice, lacking experience.

clue.text: Broadcaster with dog which went into orbit

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster
lab is short for labrador, a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A TV channel's dog that was sent into space, like the Soviet space dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: SKY is a major British pay-TV broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the American space station launched in 1973, a craft that circled the Earth.

clue.text: She soothes sensitivities of everyone tigers chewed

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: chewed means mauled, so the letters of tigers are mixed up

explanation.surface: A woman calming everyone's nerves after a tiger mauling.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor specialising in allergies treats people's sensitivities to substances.

clue.text: End power struggle for second 26

indicators.note: a struggle is a tussle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A call to end a power struggle in favour of a deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that belonged to someone before are second-hand, the same idea.

clue.text: Mass measurement finishing after a couple of minutes in Georgia

indicators.note: the pieces go in between the two letters for Georgia

parts.note: GE is the international code for the country Georgia

indicators.note: only the finishing letter of the word after is used

parts.note: M is minute, so two of them give MM

explanation.surface: A weight reading taken a couple of minutes after the finish in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing' takes R, the last letter of 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the older British spelling of the metric unit of mass, a thousandth of a kilogram.

clue.text: Inspect what used to be a colliery

parts.note: ex means former
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Inspect the site of a former coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to look at it closely, which is inspecting.

clue.text: Look into Leicester possibly being cut off by filthiness

indicators.note: the word for look goes inside the trimmed piece
the word square loses its end letter

parts.note: Leicester Square is in central London, so Leicester can precede square
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone peers into Leicester, finding it cut off and filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester Square is a famous public square in London's West End; 'being cut off' drops the final letter of the square word, and 'into' puts look inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalor is a state of dirt and neglect, so a synonym of filthiness.

clue.text: Medal for second fictional pirate

definitions.meaning: the runner-up gets a medal of the second metal after gold
Long John is the pirate in Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A pirate in a story who won a runner-up medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Second place earns this medal, and Long John of Treasure Island bears the name.

clue.text: Second part covers split

indicators.note: the word for part goes round the other piece

parts.note: a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A second part covers a crack.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two halves, so to split.

clue.text: A clue I bend deviously, which can't be taught

indicators.note: deviously means by a crooked route, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter admits bending a clue in a way nobody could learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond instruction is incapable of being educated, which is what can't be taught means.

clue.text: The Spanish mostly give off fragrant resin

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to emit is to give off

explanation.surface: The Spanish mostly give off a sweet resinous scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic gum from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfume.

clue.text: Pasta or hybrid yak

parts.note: a zo (also dzo or zho) is a cross between a yak and a cow

explanation.surface: A menu choice: pasta, or yak meat of mixed breed.
explanation.walkthrough: ZO, the yak-cow cross, is a crossword staple worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Orzo is a rice-shaped Italian pasta, an example of that food.

clue.text: Chinese director possibly minute

parts.note: the Han are the majority Chinese people

explanation.surface: A Chinese film director, possibly a small one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' is the noun-modifying sense, as in a minute hand on a clock, not tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's pointers include the one for minutes, so a minute pointer is an example of this.

clue.text: Throw out film about Japanese city

indicators.note: the film's letters go about the other pieces

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an alien
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone throws out a film set in a Japanese city.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject something is to expel it, a straight synonym of throw out.

clue.text: Independent note helping another run- through

parts.note: te is the seventh note in sol-fa
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: An independent musical note helping with a second rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: Each repetition of a process is one of these, so a further run-through.

clue.text: Time children went and turned knobs

parts.note: to widdle is a childish word for passing water, so children's word for went

explanation.surface: Bored children fiddling with the dials to pass the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' here is the nursery sense of going to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To twiddle is to twist or fiddle with something, as one does with knobs.

clue.text: Revised some quayside tidetables on the way back

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards
some of the letters of quayside tidetables are taken

explanation.surface: Some tide tables at the quay have been revised for the return trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been revised has been corrected and amended, i.e. worked over.
